summary: Tucker County, WV state station on Weiss Knob (1913-1916 warden reports); FFLA lists it gone; a ski area later used the knob's slope.

facts.agency: West Virginia Forest, Game and Fish Warden (per the reports quoted on the Eastern US lookouts page)
facts.status_note: Listed as gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association; no source describes what remains at the site or whether it is open to visitors.

events.note: Trail and telephone line construction; $137.48 expended, per the state warden's 1913-14 biennial report
Reported in the 1916 report as temporarily abandoned during the preceding year, to secure a watchman at another point; supervised by F.M. Glenn; elevation 4,490 feet

evidence.supports: station in Tucker County in the 1910s
evidence.quote: This station is located in Tucker County, and is under the supervision of F.M. Glenn.

evidence.supports: page quotes the state Forest, Game and Fish Warden reports
evidence.quote: (4th Biennial Report of the Forest, Game and Fish Warden)

evidence.supports: May 1913 entry: $137.48 on trail and telephone line construction

It is at an elevation of 4,490 feet
is under the supervision of F.M. Glenn.

evidence.quote: A watchman will probably be put on duty there again within a short time.

evidence.quote: In 1955, University of Virginia School of Law student Robert Barton established Weiss Knob Ski Area

evidence.supports: ski area climbed the slope of Weiss Knob
evidence.quote: climbing the slope of Weiss Knob above the Cabin Mountain site

evidence.supports: state acquired the original site in 1959
evidence.quote: This site was acquired by the state of West Virginia in 1959

evidence.supports: Canaan Valley Resort opened for skiing in 1971 on the original site
evidence.quote: Canaan Valley Resort opened for skiing in 1971, on the original site of Weiss Knob Ski Area.

evidence.supports: gone; no description of remains or access (status only)

corrections.why: The FFLA West Virginia list types Weiss Knob as Unknown, and the Eastern US lookouts page never uses the word tower.

notes_for_editor: The Eastern page's only history is two entries from state warden biennial reports (1913-14 and 1916). No build date is given. The 1913 line reads 'West Virgina' in the source; the story does not repeat the typo. The FFLA list types the site Unknown while our record says tower; see the proposed correction. Ski-area history comes from Wikipedia and was not checked against a primary source. Eastern page coordinates (38.99372, -79.42977) differ from FFLA (38.99389, -79.42993) by about 0.0002 degrees. The knob's access status is unknown.
